'''Andrew Gino Lumsden''' (born 22 January 1947)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | title=LUMSDEN, Prof. Andrew Gino | id = U25106 | volume = 2014 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is an [[English people|English]] [[neurobiologist]], Emeritus Professor of the [[University of London]] and founder in 2000 of the [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] Centre for Developmental Neurobiology<ref name=scopus/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kcl.ac.uk/depsta/biomedical/mrc|title=King's College London - Department of Developmental Neurobiology|website=www.kcl.ac.uk}}</ref> at [[King's College London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kcl.ac.uk/depsta/biomedical/mrc/index.php?page=http://www.kcl.ac.uk/depsta/biomedical/mrc/ResearchGroup.php?GroupID=18 |title=Lumsden Official Page |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101210214243/http://www.kcl.ac.uk/depsta/biomedical/mrc/index.php?page=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.kcl.ac.uk%2Fdepsta%2Fbiomedical%2Fmrc%2FResearchGroup.php%3FGroupID%3D18 |archive-date=10 December 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|id=7_B5hC2cxT4 |title=Andrew Lumsden talking about Neural Development journal}}</ref>

==Education==
Andrew Lumsden attended [[Kingswood School]] in [[Bath, Somerset]] (as Andrew Sita-Lumsden)<ref name=whoswho/> and graduated from [[St. Catharine's College, Cambridge]] with Double First Class Honours in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences]]. After visiting [[Yale University]] for two years as a [[Fulbright Scholar]], he returned to England to complete his [[PhD]] in Developmental Biology at the University of London.

==Career and research==
Lumsden has held various [[lecturer|lectureships]] at [[Guy's Hospital]] Medical School and the United Medical Schools of Guy's and St. Thomas' Hospital before being made a full Professor of the University of London in 1989.  He has been an International Scholar of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (1993–1998) and a [[Miller Institute]] visiting professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1994).

Lumsden has served on the Medical Research Council Neurosciences and Mental Health Board and Grants Committee (1992—1998), the [[Wellcome Trust]] Neuroscience Funding Committee (1997—2000), and the Brain Functions Grant Review Committee of the [[Human Frontier Science Program]] (1998—2001). He has also served as editor of ''[[Development (journal)|Development]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biologists.com/Development|title=Development - The Company of Biologists}}</ref> (1995—2007) and is co-founder of the on-line, open-access journal ''Neural Development''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.neuraldevelopment.com|title=Neural Development|website=Neural Development}}</ref> In addition, Andrew Lumsden is a co-Head of Section for [[Faculty of 1000]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://f1000biology.com/about/biography/1000251023259107 |title=Andrew Lumsden: Advisory Board Member in Neurodevelopment: F1000Prime |website=f1000biology.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100201160613/http://f1000biology.com/about/biography/1000251023259107 |archive-date=1 February 2010 }}</ref>

Andrew Lumsden has co-authored a book entitled ''The Developing Brain'' with Michael Brown and Roger Keynes.<ref name="The Developing Brain">{{cite book|last=Brown|first=Michael|author2=Roger Keynes |author3=Andrew Lumsden |title=The Developing Brain|publisher=Oxford University Press|date=February 14, 2002|isbn=978-0-19-854793-8}}</ref> Following his PhD on epithelial-mesenchymal interactions in mammalian development, Lumsden's interest moved to the question of how integumental structures, such as teeth and [[vibrissae]] acquire their nerve supply, and how the cranial [[neural crest]] contributes to their patterning. Studies on the development of the trigeminal nerve and ganglion led on to observations of the organisation of their corresponding motor and sensory regions of the [[central nervous system]].  His seminal observations and experiments on the developing [[Rhombencephalon|hindbrain]] of mammal and bird embryos confirmed the long suggested but never agreed view that this brain region has a rigidly segmented organisation, much like the body plan of insects and worms. To assist his research, he developed the Lumsden BioScissors™.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bio-rad.com/LifeScience/pdf/bioscissors.pdf |title=Lumsden Bioscissors™ |website=bio-rad.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726222534/http://www.bio-rad.com/LifeScience/pdf/bioscissors.pdf |archive-date=26 July 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://obanpi.co.uk |title=Obanpi |website=obanpi.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709030309/http://obanpi.co.uk/ |archive-date=9 July 2011 }}</ref> Most recently, he has focussed on the developing forebrain, where he discovered signalling properties in a small set of cells that pattern the large surrounding region of the [[thalamus]].

=== Awards and honours===
Lumsden was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (elected 1994), a [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (1998), and a [[Fellow]] of [[King's College London]] (1999).<ref name=whoswho/> He was also elected an [[EMBO Member]] in 2008.{{citation needed|date=July 2017}}

In 2001, he was awarded The [[Ferrier Lecture]] and medal by the [[Royal Society]]<ref name=frs/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/royalsoc/mee_ferr.htm |title=Royal Society prize |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030414005949/http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/royalsoc/mee_ferr.htm |archive-date=14 April 2003 }}</ref> and in 2007, the [[W. Maxwell Cowan]] Prize<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cajalclub.org/id17.html |title=Cowan and Palay Awards |website=cajalclub.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725123132/http://www.cajalclub.org/id17.html |archive-date=25 July 2011 }}</ref> for "outstanding contributions in developmental neuroscience".

Lumsden has also been elected Freeman of the [[Worshipful Company of Clockmakers]] in 2006, and raised to the Livery in 2016.<ref name=whoswho/>
